ai.title: Fix line endings in processFileBlock
ai.summary: processFileBlock now preserves original line endings in returned content and patch by moving normalization to the return step. Removed pre-normalization of updatedContent and post-normalization of patch before diff generation. Ensures consistency with normalizedInitialContent and fixes unit test failures. Affects backend/src/process-file-block.ts.

eli5.text: When the tool reads and rewrites your project files, it now keeps the exact line-break style the file originally used instead of swapping everything to one standard style. Previously the text got reformatted with mismatched breaks before the comparison was made, which produced confusing or broken results; now the comparison happens on the original text and the final output is given back with consistent line breaks. You won't see any new buttons or menus, but files you ask the tool to modify will come out closer to how they looked before, with only the parts you changed actually changed.

ai.title: Update check-new-files prompt for single-message context
ai.summary: Added instruction to read relevant files when user has only sent one message in `backend/src/find-files/check-new-files-necessary.ts`. This refines the heuristic for determining necessary file reads in the initial request phase. Scope limited to backend file-finding logic. The change ensures broader context gathering for single-turn queries.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant a question for the first time with no prior conversation, it now automatically looks at the relevant files related to your request before responding. This means that for single-message questions, the assistant gathers a bit more context from existing files to give you a better answer. You don’t have to ask it to read anything extra, it just does it on its own during that first interaction.

ai.title: Add onToolEnd newline to Read renderer
ai.summary: Added `onToolEnd` hook to `Read` tool renderer in `tool-renderers.ts`. Returns `\n` after tool execution. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/utils/tool-renderers.ts`. Note: Tests missing.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you the contents of a file, it used to stop right at the end of the text with no space before whatever came next. Now a blank line automatically appears after the file content, so the next message or block of text starts neatly separated instead of running together. If you looked, you'd see a small extra gap where file contents are displayed, making things a little easier to read.

ai.title: Tweak checkNewFilesNecessary logic
ai.summary: Updated `checkNewFilesNecessary` prompt to enforce aggressive file reading at conversation start. Removed single-message constraint from YES conditions, moved it to explicit YES directive. Added newline to `read_files` tag in `main-prompt.ts`. Covers backend file-finding logic.

eli5.text: When you start a new conversation with the assistant, it now automatically reads a broader set of files right away, even if you've only sent one message. Previously, the assistant would hold back from reading many files unless the situation clearly called for it. The change also fixes a formatting issue in how file paths are listed, making the file-reading process smoother. This is already live, so you'll notice the assistant pulling in more context from the start of your chats.

ai.title: Catch errors in websocket sendAction
ai.summary: APIRealtimeClient.sendAction now awaits sendMessage inside try/catch, logging action and error message on failure. npm-app Client.init removed its external .catch handler, relying on the centralized error capture in common/src/websockets/websocket-client.ts. Affects shared websocket layer and CLI client initialization.

eli5.text: When the app tries to send an action over the real-time connection and something goes wrong, it now logs the specific action and the error message instead of failing silently. This affects the shared communication layer used across the CLI and npm package, so errors that previously slipped through will now surface in your console as a readable 'Error sending action:' line. If you initiate the connection from the npm package client, the old inline error handler was removed in favor of this centralized logging, so you'll see consistent error output regardless of where the failure originates.

ai.title: Guard message-cost-response sends on open websocket
ai.summary: Added `ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN` check before sending `message-cost-response` in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` to prevent writes to closed sockets. `backend/src/websockets/server.ts` gains per-connection error handling and `logger.warn` calls in `deadConnectionCleaner` to catch `SWITCHBOARD.getClient` failures and log inactive terminations. Scope limited to backend websocket and cost tracking subsystems. Missing client entries now trigger explicit termination instead of silent failure.

eli5.text: When you're having a conversation with a chatbot over a live connection and the system tries to tell you how much that reply cost in credits, it now double-checks that your connection is still active before sending that message. If your connection had already dropped, instead of silently failing or causing an error, the system logs a warning so it's easier to track what happened. The same behind-the-scenes cleanup process that clears out old or broken connections now catches its own mistakes and logs them, so dropped connections are handled more carefully instead of being ignored.

ai.title: Limit bare git log to last 5 commits
ai.summary: Special case in `runTerminalCommand` (`npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`) rewrites exact `git log` to `git log -n 5`. Prevents output flooding when agent requests full history. Covers both PTY and child_process fallback paths.

eli5.text: When someone running the assistant asks it to show the full history of your project's code changes, the assistant now automatically shows only the most recent few changes instead. This prevents the screen from filling up with hundreds of lines. If you look closely, you'd see that typing the plain command to view history now quietly runs a slightly restricted version that caps the output.

ai.title: CLI parser migrated to Commander library
ai.summary: Replaced manual `process.argv` parsing with `commander` in `npm-app/src/index.ts`. Adds `commander` dependency and updates `npm-app/package.json` scripts to remove hardcoded `--git stage` flag. Enables structured help text, versioning, and option handling for flags like `--create`, `--lite`, and `--max`.

eli5.text: The assistant's way of reading your typed commands has been rebuilt from scratch. Instead of the old system that manually picked through each flag you type, it now uses a standard, purpose-built command-reading tool. You won't see anything different when you launch it, but the program now supports clean, consistent help text and version info, and the old hardcoded staging flag that used to run automatically has been removed. This is behind-the-scenes cleanup that makes the command system more reliable and easier to extend, but your daily workflow stays the same.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.192
ai.summary: Updated version in npm-app/package.json to 1.0.192. Internal release increment.

eli5.text: A new version of the software rolled out today with a set of behind-the-scenes fixes and tweaks. The biggest visible improvement is that the assistant now keeps the original formatting of text files intact when reading and editing them, so code and documents no longer get reformatted unexpectedly. Additional refinements help the assistant read the right files at the start of a conversation, handle errors more gracefully, and keep terminal commands from getting too long, all of which make responses more reliable and focused.

ai.title: Remove blank line before terminal command display
ai.summary: Removed `console.log()` calls in `runCommandPty` and `runCommandChildProcess` within `npm-app/src/utils/terminal.ts`. This eliminates the extra newline printed before the green command prompt when `mode === 'assistant'`. Affects terminal output formatting for command execution.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs a command in the terminal, it now prints the command prompt on the very next line with no extra blank line gap before it. The blank line that used to appear between commands has been removed, so the output looks slightly more compact. This only affects what you see when the assistant is showing and running terminal commands.
